purpose: Clotrimazole is used to treat fungal infections on the skin or in the body. It can clear up conditions like athlete's foot, jock itch, ringworm, and yeast infections. It comes in creams, powders, lozenges, and vaginal inserts depending on where the infection is.
how_it_works: Clotrimazole works by attacking the outer layer of the fungus, called its cell membrane. It pokes holes in that membrane, causing the fungus to leak and die. Basically, it destroys the fungus from the outside in, stopping the infection from spreading.
common_side_effects: Mild burning, stinging, or itching right where you apply it. Some redness or irritation of the skin. With vaginal forms, you might notice mild discomfort or a slight increase in discharge at first. These effects are usually short-lived.
warnings: Do not use this in your eyes. If your symptoms do not improve after 2 to 4 weeks, check back with your doctor or pharmacist. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant before using the vaginal form. Avoid using latex condoms or diaphragms right after using the vaginal cream, as the medication can weaken latex. If you have severe irritation or an allergic reaction like swelling or rash, stop using it and seek help right away.
typical_dosing: For skin infections like athlete's foot or ringworm, apply a thin layer to the affected area two times a day, usually for 2 to 4 weeks. For vaginal yeast infections, one dose of the vaginal insert at bedtime or use the cream for 3 to 7 nights depending on the product. For oral thrush using the lozenge, dissolve one lozenge slowly in your mouth 5 times a day for 14 days. Always follow the directions on your specific product.
